general_summary: Rosmaninho + Azevedo is the name of the studio formed in Porto in 2015 by Susana Rosmaninho and Pedro Azevedo. From the beginning they’re dedicated to the most diverse scales, programs and sites, showing great resilience with tight budgets and deadlines. They move in the permanent search for a synthesis, in an optimistic and pragmatic process that focuses on the essential and that often finds in the constraints an unblocking. They seek that all project challenges are opportunities to solve problems and make architecture happen. Their intention is to foster the practice of architecture with additional multi-disciplinary improvements such as museology. All projects interest them, public and private, from houses to museums, from exhibitions and small ephemeral buildings to urbanism. The common factor linking the projects and works is that they are faithful to clear formal concepts, which are complemented by easily comprehensible building strategies. We highlight the Tua Valley Interpretive Centre and the Project for the Requalification and Musealization of Casa do Passal – Aristides de Sousa Mendes (1st Prize, 2017). In addition to the distinctions in public competitions, our work has been published nationally and internationally. In 2018 the Tua Valley Interpretive Centre won the Jury’s Special Award in the Archizinc Trophy – VMZinc (Paris); it was also nominated for the EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture – Mies van der Rohe Award 2019, was a finalist in the Bauwelt Award 2019: First Works and a finalist in The Plan Award 2019. For its set of projects and works this practice was a finalist in the Architectural Review Emerging Architecture Awards (AREA) 2018. Susana Rosmaninho Architect, museologist and cultural producer. Master in Museology by the Faculty of Arts of the University of Porto (2013). Researcher at CITCEM – Transdisciplinary Research Centre «Culture, Space and Memory», since 2014. She has developed museological consulting for various entities. Collaborated between 2011 and 2012 in the curatorial assistance and production of exhibitions under the program of Art and Architecture of Guimarães 2012 European Capital of Culture. Co-founder and director of the Cultural Association Container & Content since 2015. Pedro Azevedo Master in Architecture by the Lusíada University of Porto (2009). Finalist of the Secil Architecture Award Universities 2009. Advanced Studies Course in Architectural Heritage by the Faculty of Architecture of the University of Porto (2018). Fellow of the Santa María la Real Foundation (2010). Collaborated between 2010 and 2015 with Menos é Mais Architects (Cristina Guedes + Francisco Vieira de Campos). Co-founder of the Cultural Association Container & Content (2015).

Francisco Portugal e Gomes was born on the 10th of July, 1963 in Oporto, Portugal. In 1983 enters the Architecture Course of Belas Artes in Oporto. In 1989 gets the graduate degree in Architecture by the FAUP - Architecture Faculty of Oporto University. Between 1988 and 1997 cooperates with the architects Jorge Gigante, Francisco Melo, José Gigante and João Álvaro Rocha in their own's office. From 1992 to 1995 was pointed out as collaborator in two projects of architects José Gigante and João Álvaro Rocha's authorship: LNIV - National Laboratory of Veterinary Investigation in Varão, Vila do Conde and ICP - Institute of the Portuguese Comunications/ North Delegation. The first work received the Prize for the European Section of the American Institute of Architects (AIA) in 2001 and the second was awarded with the Prize Architecti/ Centro Cultural de Belém in 1995. From 1994 to 2000, Francisco Portugal e Gomes performed several projects in co-authorship with architect João Álvaro Rocha. From 2001 on works as architect in his own office located in Oporto, Portugal. Between 1995, and 1997, teached as invited assistant in the FAUP - Architecture Faculty of Oporto University. Since 2005 works in the ESG/ Escola Superior Gallaecia, teaching Urban and Rural Rehabilitation to the 5th degree of the Architecture Course. In 1991 receives the secound prize in the Restricted Contest, Municipal Public Library in Santo Tirso. In 2004 is also awarded with the 2nd Prize in the Restricted Contest concerning the Touristic Undertaking Quinta Vale Covo. In 2006, receives the 4 th Honourable Mention in the International Contest of the Bridge-Museum Academy, Venice, Italy. In co-authorship with architect João Álvaro Rocha wins several prizes: Honourable Mention in the Public Contest for the Cultural Building in the Enclosure of Palácio de Cristal, Oporto, 1994; first Prize in the Restricted Contest by Previous Qualification for the Universitary Student's Dwelling of the Universitary Pole in Alto da Ajuda, Lisbon, 1996; first Prize in the contest for the Conception/ Construction of the Urban Park in Moutidos, Maia, 1997. In the year 2000, he is also finalist of the Premis FAD/Barcelona - Architecture Section, with the Residential Complex of Outeiro I, from the P.E.R. Program of the Town Hall of Maia.

António Pedro Faria has a Master degree in Architecture from Faculty of Architecture of the University of Porto. In 2017 he makes in co-authorship with the architects LACATON & VASSAL the “Invited International Competition for the Rehabilitation of Portugalia’s Block” and the “Competition for the Rehabilitation of the Lycee Français Charles Lepierre”, also in co-authorship with the architects LACATON & VASSAL and Nuno Valentim. Member of the Portuguese Architects Association (no24581), made an internship at LACATON&VASSAL, in Paris (2016) and ATELIERMOB, in Lisbon (2016-2017). He worked in ATELIERDATA, in Lisbon (2017-1019). In 2019 he won a Scholarship for outstanding application to participate in the international workshop “Creating Homes for Tomorrow”, organized by Canactions School and held in Amsterdam, Zurich, Helsinki and Kiev. In 2016, gets the 2nd place for a ideas competition to the reabilitation of an housing complex in the historical centre of Braga (Portugal). Before that period, he worked for Lisbon Architecture Trienalle and the Portuguese Directorate General of Arts as a copy-editor for the Oficial Portuguese Representation at Venice Architecture Biennale 2014, with the name :”Homeland: news from Portugal”. general_summary: Brandão Costa Lima Founded by Amélia Brandão Costa and Rodrigo da Costa Lima in 2007. Since then they have designed a very different range of projects from very small scale projects, as furniture and villas, to public buildings or urban plans. Their work has been presented and awarded. This website is a selection of what they have been doing. Amélia Brandão Costa Graduated in Architecture at ULP, Porto in 2004. She also studied at Staatliche Akademie der Bildenden Künste Stuttgart and she won the first prize by Domus magazine for a MA in Design at Domus Academy in Milan. Before establishing her own office in 2007 with Rodrigo da Costa Lima she learned from João Pedro Serôdio, Isabel Furtado, Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron. Her works and writings have been published and presented on lectures and exhibitions. She is founder and director of 'Indexnewspaper' and 'Porto Academy'. Rodrigo da Costa Lima Graduated in Architecture at ULP, Porto, in 2003. Before establishing his own office in 2007 with Amélia Brandão Costa he learned from João Pedro Serôdio, Isabel Furtado, Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron. His works and writings have been published and presented on lectures and exhibitions. He is founder and director of 'Indexnewspaper' and 'Porto Academy'.

Vasco is a native of Lisbon and began his artistic studies at the António Arroio School. He graduated from Lusíada University in Lisbon and moved to the North, completing his master's degree at the Porto School of Art. Along the way, he established numerous personal and professional relationships throughout the region and explored the diverse ways of practicing and understanding this craft in different regions. After spending five years in the job market, gaining experience through collaborations with various offices, the opportunity arose in 2019 to pursue the craft independently. "In this order, my architecture comes: from the place, the developer, the local society, and only then, the author. Thus, the categorization of a "style" or a "language" does not exist. In this methodology, there are no styles. The client's intention is pursued and the constraints are managed in that same order."
